story:
I have hunted bears my whole life. Alongside my dad and my good friend Dan, we ran baits and followed the dogs through the woods. I had worked the same bait site since the late 1990s and had passed on many bears over the years. We shared plenty of great chases and lasting memories, yet I had never taken a bear I felt was truly worthy.

Coming into that season, I decided it was time. I could not wait forever. All I wanted was a mature boar. I was coaching baseball at the time and had only a narrow window between the district tournament and state—where our team would go on to finish second.

It was a cold, snowy morning in May. A nice boar had been working the bait. The dogs had circled a couple of times, and we knew they were on a bear, but they could not get it treed. We decided to push in and see what was happening. We found the dogs driving a chocolate-colored bear across the ridge. Finally they put him up a tree.

It was an outstanding first bear—squared close to six feet, though the skull measured a modest seventeen inches. That hunt would be the last one I ever shared with Dan before he passed away.
